questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman presented with a malodorous, green-yellow vaginal discharge. On cervical evaluation the cervix had an erythematous, punctate, and papilliform appearance. Investigations: Microscopy of the vaginal fluid: NAAT testing for gonorrhea and chlamydia negative
questions.lead_in: What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.explanation: Metronidazole × 1 dose This is Trichomonas infection, as confirmed by the flagellated protozoan organism on microscopy. Trichomonas vaginalis should be treated with metronidazole 2 g for one dose. Alternative regimens include metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. Rescreening should be performed in 3 months because reinfection is common. (Image from Gardella C, Eckert LO, Lentz GM. Genital tract infections. In Lobo RA, Gershenson DM, Lentz GM, Valea F , eds. Comprehensive Gynecology. 7th ed. Elsevier; 2017.)
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 4 Q24

questions.question: A woman has refractory Trichomonas vaginalis infection unresponsive to metronidazole.
questions.question_raw: Woman with refractory trichomonas infection that is unresponsive to metronidazole

parts.text: Give three reasons why the organism may be "resistant."

parts_raw.text: Give 3 reasons why the organism may be "resistant"?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Reinfection from an untreated male sexual partner — failure to treat the partner is the most common cause of recurrent disease and should be excluded before assuming a truly resistant strain. (2) Relative (dose-dependent) resistance that can usually be overcome with higher oral doses; there is no reliable correlation between in vitro and in vivo resistance. (3) True metronidazole resistance (estimated 2.5–10%), mediated by reduced expression of hydrogenosomal enzymes (pyruvate ferredoxin oxidoreductase, ferredoxin, malic enzyme, hydrogenase) impairing drug activation, and by mutations in nitroreductase genes.

cohort_answer.text: Non-compliance - most common cause (use single dose therapy); Reinfection by partners; True resistance - ultra rare (unlikely; if true failure on single dose try metronidazole 500mg PO bid x7 days for rare flagyl resistance [4%]; if fails try in vitro culture/susceptibility; if truly flagyl resistant try Tinidazole)

questions.question: A woman has refractory Trichomonas vaginalis infection unresponsive to metronidazole.
questions.question_raw: Woman with refractory trichomonas infection that is unresponsive to metronidazole

parts.text: How would you treat this patient?

parts_raw.text: How would you treat this patient?

questions.model_answer: a) First ensure the male partner is treated and adherence confirmed, as untreated partners are the commonest cause of recurrence. For patients failing a single 2-g dose of metronidazole, the CDC recommendation is metronidazole 500 mg PO twice daily for 7 days, or tinidazole 2 g PO immediately. If that fails, treat with tinidazole or metronidazole 2 g PO daily for 5 days; tinidazole (more favorable pharmacokinetics) is the drug of choice when resistance is encountered, with high-dose oral plus intravaginal tinidazole (2–3 g PO plus 1–1.5 g intravaginally for 14 days) achieving ~92% cure in refractory cases. If true metronidazole allergy is present, desensitization is required as there is no effective alternative.

cohort_answer.text: Re-treat with metronidazole single dose and treat partners. Efficacy 82-88%, increases to 95% if partner also treated. First line: Metronidazole 2g PO single dose, or 500mg PO bid x7 days; or Tinidazole 2g PO once (or 2g daily x7 days). If allergic, need desensitizing due to poor efficacy of alternatives

questions.question: State the preferred therapy for the following infection.
questions.model_answer: a) A single 2-g oral dose of metronidazole (or tinidazole), with routine treatment of sexual partners; reported cure rates are 90–100%.

cohort_answer.text: Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x7 days OR 2g PO x1

questions.question: Name the first-line treatment regimen for the following infections in men who have sex with men, as per the Public Health Agency of Canada.
questions.question_raw: Name the first-line treatment regimen for the following infections in men who have sex with men, as per the Public Health Agency of Canada.
questions.model_answer: a) Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose plus azithromycin 1 g PO single dose. b) Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO single dose alternative). c) Azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1 then 250 mg daily for 4 days (or doxycycline lead-in), with moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily for 7–14 days for macrolide-resistant/persistent disease. d) Metronidazole 2 g PO single dose (or 500 mg PO bid for 7 days). e) Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO alternative).
questions.beyond_mandell: Regimens are from the PHAC Canadian Guidelines on Sexually Transmitted Infections; the chapter (CDC-based) does not give Canada-specific MSM regimens.

questions.question: Based on PHAC guidelines, name the recommended first-line treatment (drug, dose, route, duration) for each of the following in the MSM population.
questions.question_raw: Based on PHAC guidelines, name the recommended first-line treatment for the following for the MSM community (drug, dose, route, duration).
questions.model_answer: a) Neisseria gonorrhoeae: ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose PLUS azithromycin 1 g PO single dose. b) Chlamydia trachomatis: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO single dose alternative; LGV treated x21 days). c) Trichomonas vaginalis: metronidazole 2 g PO single dose. d) Mycoplasma genitalium: azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1 then 250 mg PO daily to complete 5 days. e) Ureaplasma urealyticum: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x7 days.
questions.beyond_mandell: Doses/durations are from PHAC Canadian Guidelines on STIs (MSM); this chapter follows CDC and does not tabulate PHAC MSM regimens.

cohort_answer.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Ceftriaxone 250mg IM once PLUS Azithromycin 1g PO once. Chlamydia trachomatis: Doxycycline 100mg PO bid x7 days (for LGV treat 21d). Trichomonas vaginalis: Metronidazole 2g PO once. Mycoplasma genitalium: Azithromycin 500mg PO day 1 followed by 250mg PO for total of 5d. Ureaplasma urealyticum: Doxycycline 100mg PO bid x7 days
